content: Magnesium carbonate is a compound that is FDA-approved for the treatment of indigestion. It is primarily used to provide temporary relief from upset stomach, sour stomach, and acid indigestion. The recommended dosage for magnesium hydroxide liquid, when used as an antacid, is 400 to 1200 milligrams taken orally up to four times daily. For elemental magnesium, the recommended dose is 6 milligrams taken orally daily with food. There is limited information available regarding the off-label use of magnesium carbonate in adult patients, whether supported or unsupported by clinical guidelines. Similarly, there is limited data on its FDA-labeled or off-label use in pediatric patients. Magnesium carbonate should not be used by individuals with kidney disease. It is also important not to exceed the maximum recommended daily dose (8 teaspoons for adults and 4 teaspoons for children) or to use the maximum dosage for more than two weeks unless under the advice and supervision of a physician. The product may have a laxative effect, and antacids, including magnesium carbonate, may interact with certain prescription medications. In the event of an accidental overdose, professional assistance or contact with a Poison Control Center should be sought immediately. Adverse reactions to magnesium carbonate are not well-documented in clinical trials or post-marketing data. Similarly, there is limited information regarding drug interactions, monitoring, and administration of magnesium carbonate. There is no FDA guidance on its use during pregnancy, labor and delivery, or in nursing mothers. Additionally, there is no specific guidance for its use in pediatric, geriatric, gender-specific, racial, renal-impaired, hepatic-impaired, or immunocompromised populations. Magnesium carbonate is not well-studied in terms of its pharmacology, including its mechanism of action, pharmacodynamics, pharmacokinetics, or nonclinical toxicology. Clinical studies on this compound are also limited. Information on its storage, supply, and intravenous compatibility is similarly scarce. For patient use, the medication should be shaken well before use. Adults and children aged 12 years and older are advised to take 2 teaspoons every 3 to 4 hours. Children aged 6 to 12 years should take 1 teaspoon every 3 to 4 hours. For children under 2 years of age, a doctor should be consulted before use. The interaction between alcohol and magnesium carbonate has not been established. Patients are advised to consult their doctor regarding the effects of consuming alcohol while taking this medication.
